suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-31 adds this relationship only as a bounded anorectal-function association. Anismus (dyssynergic defecation) is a functional defecation disorder defined by paradoxical contraction or failed relaxation of the pelvic floor and anal musculature during attempted defecation, and it coexists with fecal incontinence in anorectal-disorder clinical evidence, but the primary diagnosis alone does not establish incontinence in every person or determine an individual's course. Require independently documented dyssynergia by anorectal manometry and balloon-expulsion testing, documented fecal incontinence by validated assessment compatible in chronology, and specialist review. Preserve obstetric injury, prior anorectal surgery, neurologic disease, diabetes, and other competing causes of fecal incontinence.

sourceReferences.citation: Rao SSC, Bharucha AE, Carrington EV, Grossi U, Malcolm A, Neshatian L, Remes-Troche JM. Anorectal Disorders. Gastroenterology. 2026;170(6):1318-1346. PMID 41713710. doi:10.1053/j.gastro.2026.01.037.
sourceReferences.note: AGA-affiliated clinical review defining diagnostic criteria and clinical evaluation for dyssynergic defecation and fecal incontinence within the anorectal-disorder spectrum. It supports a bounded disease-association proposition and clinical evaluation, not automatic individual causation or aggravation.
sourceReferences.sourceLocator: PMID 41713710; anorectal-disorder criteria covering dyssynergic defecation and fecal incontinence

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Dyssynergic defecation and fecal incontinence coexist within the anorectal-disorder spectrum and share pelvic-floor neuromuscular dysfunction, but the clinical-review evidence does not establish an individual medical nexus without documentation of both disorders, compatible chronology, and competing-cause review.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation under 38 CFR § 3.310 is established by this association evidence; the mapping is not an individual nexus opinion.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Shared pelvic-floor neuromuscular incoordination is hypothesized to impair both evacuation and continence, but the individual pathway must be established from manometry, endoanal imaging, and specialist pelvic-floor evaluation.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: This relationship is supported as an association only. Dyssynergic defecation and fecal incontinence are defined within the same anorectal-disorder framework and can coexist, but the review evidence does not establish that anismus caused or aggravated fecal incontinence in every individual; both diagnoses, chronology, objective findings, and competing etiologies require case-specific review.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Objective dyssynergia and incontinence documentation; chronology; manometric and imaging findings; obstetric, surgical, neurologic, and metabolic alternatives; specialist assessment of the individual relationship
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Obstetric anal-sphincter injury or prior anorectal surgery
Neurologic disease or diabetes-related autonomic dysfunction
Primary sphincter weakness or structural anorectal disease
